title: Sounding natural
goal: Ask people to repeat or slow down, ask what a word means, react like a native ('no way!', 'I swear!'), add 'right?' to a sentence, put emphasis where you want it, use echo words, and mix in English the way young Pashtuns do.
intro:
Textbook Pashto gets the message across; real Pashto is full of little words that carry the feeling: **کنه** 'right?', **خو** 'come on, but', **هم** 'even', **توبه!** 'good grief!', **په خدای!** 'I swear!', echo words like **چای مای** 'tea and stuff', and a sprinkle of English — ټېنشن، پرابلم، اوکې.

This unit gives you those words, plus the survival lines every learner needs: 'say that again', 'slow down', 'what does that mean?', 'what do you call this in Pashto?'.

grammar.title: Tag questions: … نه؟ · … کنه؟ · … که نه؟
grammar.body:
English has 'isn't it?', 'don't you?', 'right?'. Pashto has a few short tags that never change, whatever the verb:

**نه؟** (na) at the end of a statement: 'right?' — you expect 'yes': ته به سبا راشې، **نه؟** 'you'll come tomorrow, right?'

**کنه** (kəna, unit 21) is warmer and very common. After a statement it asks for agreement — 'isn't it, don't you': ته پښتون يې **کنه**؟ 'you're Pashtun, aren't you?'. Without a question mark it means 'obviously, you know': ما خو درته ويلي وو **کنه** 'I told you, didn't I'. As an answer, **هو کنه!** means 'yes, of course!'.

**که نه؟** (ka na) 'or not?' checks or pushes for a decision: راځې **که نه**؟ 'are you coming or not?'. Slightly impatient.

**سمه ده؟ / اوکې؟** 'OK?' after a suggestion or instruction.

Answering: **هو** / **هو کنه** 'yes'; **نه** / **نه خير** 'no' (نه خير is more polite). To a negative tag question, Pashto agrees with the words, not the facts: — ته نه ځې، نه؟ — **هو** (I'm not going) / **نه، ځم** (no, I am going).

**The trap:** don't build English-style tags with a verb ("دی، نه دی؟"). The tag is always one of these fixed little words.

examples.en: Are you coming or not? I can't wait any longer.

grammar.title: Emphasis: خو، هم، لا، بس، خپله
grammar.body:
Pashto adds feeling with small words, most of them clitic-like, sitting right after the word they stress.

**خو** (xo) — besides 'but', it adds insistence or 'after all': زه **خو** درته وايم! 'but I'm *telling* you!', ته **خو** ډاکټر يې 'you're a doctor, after all'. After a command it means 'come on!': راشه **خو**! 'come on, come!'.

**هم** (ham) — 'also', but after a small amount or with a negative it means **'even'**: يوه روپۍ **هم** نه لرم 'I haven't got even one rupee', هغه دا **هم** نه پوهېږي 'he doesn't even know this'.

**لا** (lā) 'still, yet' — before a comparative it means 'even (more)': **لا** ښه 'even better', **لا** بد 'even worse'.

**بس** (bas) 'that's it, enough, just': **بس**، ځو 'right, let's go', **بس** کړه! 'stop it!', بس يو چای 'just one tea'.

**خپله** (xpə́la) 'myself, yourself, himself' for emphasis: ما **خپله** وليدل 'I saw it myself'.

**Word order** also stresses: move the important word to the front. پرون مې احمد وليد (neutral) → **احمد** مې پرون وليد 'it was *Ahmad* I saw yesterday'.

**The trap:** خو and هم go **after** the word they stress, never before it: زه **خو**, not خو زه, when you mean 'I, for my part'. (خو at the start of a sentence just means 'but'.)

grammar.title: Echo words and doubled words
grammar.body:
**Echo words.** To say 'X and that sort of thing', repeat a word and replace its first sound with **م** (m): **چای مای** 'tea and stuff', **ډوډۍ موډۍ** 'food and all that', **کتاب متاب** 'books and things', **فلم ملم** 'films and whatever'. It is casual and friendly — great with friends, out of place in a formal letter. It can also sound dismissive: پيسې ميسې نه غواړم 'I don't want money or anything'.

**Fixed pairs** you should learn as single words: **ګډ وډ** 'messy, chaotic', **کټ مټ** 'exactly the same', **شور ماشور** 'racket', **ګپ شپ** 'chit-chat' (unit 20).

**Doubling** a word adds a meaning:
- 'gradually / one by one': **ورو ورو** 'slowly, little by little', **لږ لږ** 'bit by bit', **يو يو** 'one by one'
- 'repeatedly / intensely': **ژر ژر** 'quickly, quickly', **بيا بيا** 'again and again'
- 'here and there': **ځای ځای** 'in places'

**The trap:** echo words are for nouns and everyday things; don't echo names of people or anything you want to treat with respect.

dialogue.title: Half English, half Pashto
dialogue.setting: The canteen at the University of Peshawar. Emma, who is learning Pashto, meets her friend Mursal between classes.

culture:
**Accents.** In Peshawar, Mardan and Swat you'll hear the 'hard' northern pronunciation: ښ sounds like x and ږ like g, so پښتو is *paxto*, ښه is *xə* and موږ is *mug*; څ and ځ often become s and z. Kandahar speech is softer and closer to the standard you're learning; Kabul Pashto mixes in many Dari words (برق, صاحب خانه). Nobody will mind your accent — but saying **ستا لهجه ښکلې ده** 'your accent is lovely' to a speaker from another region is a nice compliment.

**English mixing.** Educated young Pashtuns, especially in Pakistan and in the diaspora, mix in English all the time: an English noun plus a Pashto verb — ټېنشن اخيستل, چېک کول, کېنسل شو, پرابلم نشته, اوکې. It's normal among friends, but older people may tease it as showing off; with elders, use the Pashto word (ستونزه, لغوه, سمه ده).

**Swearing an oath.** **په خدای!** and **په قرآن!** 'I swear by the Quran' are said in everyday speech to show you're serious — the second is heavy and best left to native speakers. **چوپ شه** 'shut up' is only for close friends; to ask someone politely to be quiet, say **غلی شه** or **لږ غلي شئ**.

tip.title: Survival lines
tip.body:
- Repeat: **بيا يې ووايه** (informal) / **بيا يې ووايئ** (polite).
- Slower: **ورو ورو** — doubling ورو makes it 'nice and slow'.
- 'I didn't get it': **پوه نه شوم** (woman: پوه نه شوه).
- Nobody minds being asked; they'll be pleased you're trying.

tip.title: When you don't know the word
tip.body:
- Ask: **دې ته په پښتو کې څه وايي؟** (pointing), **د … معنا څه ده؟**
- Describe it: **هغه شی چې …** 'the thing that …', **لکه …** 'like …'.
- Ask for English: **په انګرېزي يې څه وايي؟**

tip.title: Tags: نه؟ · کنه؟ · که نه؟
tip.body:
- Statement + **نه؟** = 'right?'.
- **کنه؟** = 'isn't it, don't you' (warm); **هو کنه!** 'of course!'.
- **که نه؟** = 'or not?' (impatient).
- They never change — no verb in the tag.

tip.title: Reactions
tip.body:
- Surprise: **واقعاً؟**، **څه وايې!**، **په خدای؟**
- Shock or disapproval: **توبه!**، **خدايه!**
- Tired, hot, fed up: **اوف!**
- **چوپ شه** 'shut up' only with close friends.

sentences.native: واقعاً ډېر ښه سړی دی.
sentences.roman: wāqiʿán ḍer ṣə saṛáy day.
sentences.en: He's a really nice guy.

tip.title: Emphasis: خو، هم، لا، بس
tip.body:
- **خو** after a word = insistence: زه **خو** درته وايم!
- **هم** with a negative = 'even': يوه روپۍ **هم** نه لرم.
- **لا** ښه 'even better'; **بس** 'that's it, just'.
- They come right **after** the word they stress.

sentences.native: ته خو زما ملګری يې!
sentences.roman: tə xo zmā malgə́ray ye!
sentences.en: But you're my friend!

sentences.native: هغه زما نوم هم نه پوهېږي.
sentences.roman: haġá zmā num ham na pohéẓi.
sentences.en: He doesn't even know my name.

sentences.native: يو ګيلاس اوبه هم يې رانه کړې.
sentences.roman: yaw gilā́s obə́ ham ye rā́na kṛe.
sentences.en: He didn't even give me a glass of water.

sentences.native: دا لا بد شو!
sentences.roman: dā lā bad shu!
sentences.en: That's even worse!

sentences.native: بس، نور نه شم خوړلای.
sentences.roman: bas, nor na shəm xwaṛə́lāy.
sentences.en: That's it, I can't eat any more.

sentences.native: هله ژر شه، بس ځي!
sentences.roman: hála zhər sha, bas dzi!
sentences.en: Come on, hurry, the bus is leaving!

sentences.native: راشه خو، ټول ستا انتظار کوي!
sentences.roman: rā́sha xo, ṭol stā intizā́r kawí!
sentences.en: Come on, everyone's waiting for you!

sentences.native: هو، همداسې ده.
sentences.roman: ho, hamdā́se da.
sentences.en: Yes, that's exactly it.

sentences.native: ما خو همداسې يوه خبره وکړه.
sentences.roman: mā xo hamdā́se yáwa xabə́ra wə́kṛa.
sentences.en: I was just saying, that's all.

tip.title: Echo words and doubles
tip.body:
- **م**-echo = 'and stuff': **چای مای**، **ډوډۍ موډۍ**، **کتاب متاب** — casual.
- Fixed pairs: **ګډ وډ** 'messy', **کټ مټ** 'exactly'.
- Doubling: **ورو ورو** 'slowly', **لږ لږ** 'bit by bit', **بيا بيا** 'again and again'.

sentences.native: ډوډۍ موډۍ دې خوړلې؟
sentences.roman: ḍoḍə́y moḍə́y de xwaṛə́le?
sentences.en: Have you eaten anything?

sentences.native: کتاب متاب يې نه لوست، ټوله ورځ يې فلمونه کتل.
sentences.roman: kitā́b mitā́b ye na lwast, ṭóla wradz ye filmúna katə́l.
sentences.en: He didn't read books or anything — he watched films all day.

sentences.native: ستا کوټه تل ګډ وډ وي.
sentences.roman: stā kóṭa tal gaḍ waḍ wi.
sentences.en: Your room is always a mess.

sentences.native: دا کټ مټ هغه شی دی چې ما غوښت.
sentences.roman: dā kaṭ maṭ haġá shay day che mā ġwəṣt.
sentences.en: This is exactly what I wanted.

sentences.native: ورو ورو، هر څه به سم شي.
sentences.roman: wro wro, har tsə ba sam shi.
sentences.en: Bit by bit, everything will be fine.

sentences.native: بيا بيا مې زنګ ورته ووهه، خو ځواب يې نه راکاوه.
sentences.roman: biyā́ biyā́ me zang wárta wə́waha, xo dzawā́b ye na rākāwə́.
sentences.en: I called him again and again, but he wasn't answering.

sentences.native: خلاصه، هغه ورځ هر څه ګډ وډ شول.
sentences.roman: xulāsá, haġá wradz har tsə gaḍ waḍ shwəl.
sentences.en: Long story short, that day everything went wrong.

sentences.native: لږ لږ په پښتو پوهېږم.
sentences.roman: ləẓ ləẓ pə paṣtó pohéẓəm.
sentences.en: I'm starting to understand Pashto bit by bit.

tip.title: English noun + Pashto verb
tip.body:
- Young people borrow the English word and add a Pashto verb: **چېک کول**، **ټېنشن اخيستل**، **کېنسل کېدل**.
- The Pashto grammar stays: چېک **يې کړه**، کېنسل **شو**.
- With elders, use the Pashto word: ستونزه، لغوه، سمه ده.

sentences.native: اوکې، سبا وينو.
sentences.roman: okáy, sabā́ winu.
sentences.en: OK, see you tomorrow.

sentences.native: ټکټونه دې چېک کړل؟
sentences.roman: ṭikaṭúna de chek kṛəl?
sentences.en: Did you check the tickets?

sentences.native: لالا، لږ يې چېک کړه، ښايي غلط وي.
sentences.roman: lālā́, ləẓ ye chek kṛa, ṣāyí ġalát wi.
sentences.en: Bro, check it, it might be wrong.

sentences.native: ازموينې ته لا ډېر وخت دی، ټېنشن مه اخله.
sentences.roman: azmóyəne ta lā ḍer waxt day, ṭénshən ma axla.
sentences.en: The exam's still ages away — don't stress.

sentences.native: ټېنشن مې دی، کار مې لا خلاص نه دی.
sentences.roman: ṭénshən me day, kār me lā xlās na day.
sentences.en: I'm stressed — my work's still not done.

sentences.native: څه پرابلم دی، لالا؟
sentences.roman: tsə prāblə́m day, lālā́?
sentences.en: What's the problem, bro?

sentences.native: پرابلم دا دی چې پيسې نه لرم.
sentences.roman: prāblə́m dā day che páyse na lárəm.
sentences.en: The problem is I've got no money.

sentences.native: سمه ده، اوکې، زه به يې چېک کړم.
sentences.roman: sáma da, okáy, zə ba ye chek kṛəm.
sentences.en: All right, OK, I'll check it.
